1.en: You will hear a woman phoning the owner of a house she is going to rent about companies that she could rent furniture from.
1.zh: 你會聽到一位女士打電話給她即將租住房子的屋主，詢問可以租用家具的公司。

1.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.
1.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 1 至 5 題。

1.en: Now, listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.
1.zh: 現在，請仔細聆聽並回答第 1 至 5 題。

1.en: MAN: Good morning.
1.zh: 男士：早安。

1.en: SHELLEY: Hi. This is Shelley Mayer.
1.zh: Shelley：你好，我是 Shelley Mayer。

1.en: I'm renting your house on Archwood Avenue. I'm due to move in next week.
1.zh: 我租了你在 Archwood Avenue 的房子，預計下週搬進去。

1.en: MAN: Oh yes, hello Ms Mayer. What can I do for you?
1.zh: 男士：哦，是的，你好，Mayer 女士。有什麼我可以幫忙的嗎？

1.en: SHELLEY: When I viewed the house, I told you I'll most probably need to rent some furniture – at least until I know whether my temporary work contract is going to be made permanent.
1.zh: Shelley：我看房時跟你說過， 我很可能需要租一些家具—— 至少在我知道臨時工作合約是否會轉為永久合約之前。

1.en: MAN: Yes of course, I remember. And I said I could give you some information about furniture rental companies in the city.
1.zh: 男士：是的，我當然記得。我也說過可以給你一些市內家具租賃公司的資訊。

1.en: SHELLEY: That's right.
1.zh: Shelley：沒錯。

1.en: MAN: Well, the biggest company is called Peak Rentals.
1.zh: 男士：嗯，最大的一家公司叫 Peak Rentals。

1.en: I've recommended them to other people and have always heard positive reports about them.
1.zh: 我曾向其他人推薦過他們，而且一直聽到不錯的評價。

1.en: SHELLEY: Could you give me an idea of their costs?
1.zh: Shelley：你能大概告訴我他們的收費嗎？

1.en: MAN: Sure, I actually have one of their brochures here.
1.zh: 男士：當然，我這裡剛好有一本他們的小冊子。

1.en: It says the monthly price per room starts at a hundred and five dollars and goes up to two hundred and thirty-nine dollars – that depends on which rooms you need furniture for, of course.
1.zh: 上面寫著每個房間每月的價格從 105 美元起，最高到 239 美元——當然，這取決於你哪些房間需要家具。

1.en: SHELLEY: Sure. It's just to get a general idea of how much it's gonna cost.
1.zh: Shelley：明白。我只是想大概了解一下會花多少錢。

1.en: And you said you had some positive feedback about this company.
1.zh: 你剛才說這家公司有一些正面的評價。

1.en: MAN: Yes, people have mentioned that the furniture from Peak Rentals is more modern than any of the other companies.
1.zh: 男士：是的，有人提到 Peak Rentals 的家具比其他公司的都更現代。

1.en: And also, once you place an order, the furniture will be delivered to you in just one or two days.
1.zh: 而且，一旦下單，家具只要一兩天就會送到。

1.en: SHELLEY: That would be really helpful.
1.zh: Shelley：那真的很方便。

1.en: MAN: Oh, and the brochure says that there's a special offer at the moment.
1.zh: 男士：哦，還有，小冊子上說目前有一項特別優惠。

1.en: If you rent living room furniture – I believe that's a set of chairs and a TV table, you'll also get a lamp at no extra cost.
1.zh: 如果你租客廳家具——我想是一組椅子和一張電視桌——你還可以免費獲得一盞燈。

1.en: SHELLEY: OK. But, you know, that price range you gave is more than I was hoping to pay.
1.zh: Shelley：好的。不過你知道，你剛才說的價格範圍比我原本希望支付的還高。

1.en: MAN: Then you could try Aaron and Oliver.
1.zh: 男士：那你可以試試 Aaron and Oliver。

1.en: SHELLEY: Sorry, what and Oliver?
1.zh: Shelley：抱歉，什麼 and Oliver ？

1.en: MAN: Aaron. Double-A-R-O-N.
1.zh: 男士：Aaron。兩個 A，R-O-N。

1.en: SHELLEY: OK. Are they cheaper?
1.zh: Shelley：好的。他們比較便宜嗎？

1.en: MAN: I'd say they're a mid-price company.
1.zh: 男士：我會說他們是中等價位的公司。

1.en: But if you chose them, you need to be aware that they charge an extra twelve per cent every month in case of damage.
1.zh: 但如果你選他們，要注意他們每月會額外收取 12% 的費用， 以防家具受損。

1.en: SHELLEY: Oh I see. I'd have to do the math carefully then.
1.zh: Shelley：哦，我明白了。那我得仔細算一下。

1.en: MAN: Right. But one helpful thing is that they also do cleaning for customers.
1.zh: 男士：對。不過有一點很方便， 他們也為顧客提供清潔服務。

1.en: SHELLEY: For the furniture?
1.zh: Shelley：清潔家具嗎？

1.en: MAN: For the house.
1.zh: 男士：是清潔房子。

1.en: SHELLEY: Oh I see. I probably won't need that.
1.zh: Shelley：哦，我明白了。我大概不需要那個。

1.en: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.
1.zh: 在你聽接下來的對話之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 6 至 10 題。

1.en: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.
1.zh: 現在請聆聽並回答第 6 至 10 題。

1.en: MAN: There's another company called Larch Furniture.
1.zh: 男士：還有另一家公司叫 Larch Furniture。

1.en: It's quite new, and it has the lowest prices in town.
1.zh: 它相當新，而且價格是城裡最低的。

1.en: That's for both furniture and also electronic equipment.
1.zh: 這包括家具，也包括電子設備。

1.en: SHELLEY: Well that would be good.
1.zh: Shelley：那挺好的。

1.en: I'm not bringing much with me, and I won't have much time to go shopping after I start my job.
1.zh: 我不會帶太多東西過來，而且開始工作後也沒有太多時間去購物。

1.en: MAN: There are two things you need to know about Larch Furniture.
1.zh: 男士：關於 Larch Furniture， 有兩件事你需要知道。

1.en: First of all, you have to take out insurance on the furniture, and you need to organise that yourself.
1.zh: 首先，你必須為家具購買保險，而且需要自己安排。

1.en: SHELLEY: That wouldn't be too hard.
1.zh: Shelley：那應該不會太難。

1.en: MAN: Also, you can't take out a contract for less than six months, but I figure that might not be a problem for you.
1.zh: 男士：另外，你不能簽少於六個月的合約，不過我想這對你來說可能不是問題。

1.en: You're renting the house for twelve months after all, aren't you?
1.zh: 畢竟你要租這棟房子 12 個月，對吧？

1.en: SHELLEY: Yes. OK, well I …
1.zh: Shelley：是的。好的，那我……

1.en: MAN: … sorry to interrupt. I just thought of another furniture rental company.
1.zh: 男士：……抱歉打斷你。我剛想到另一家家具租賃公司。

1.en: It's called Space Rentals. And it's located very near to the house.
1.zh: 它叫 Space Rentals，而且離這棟房子很近。

1.en: SHELLEY: OK.
1.zh: Shelley：好的。

1.en: MAN: I don't have any information about their charges, so it's best to use their app to find out what it would cost you to use them.
1.zh: 男士：我沒有他們收費的資料，所以最好使用他們的應用程式查看使用他們服務需要多少費用。

1.en: SHELLEY: OK thanks. I'll do that.
1.zh: Shelley：好的，謝謝。我會這麼做。

1.en: MAN: One good thing about that company is that if you don't like the furniture once it's delivered, you can request exchanges – as long as you do that within a week of receiving it.
1.zh: 男士：那家公司有一個好處是，如果家具送到後你不喜歡， 可以要求更換——只要你在收到家具後一週內提出。

1.en: SHELLEY: That sounds really great. OK. Well thanks very much. That's so helpful …
1.zh: Shelley：聽起來真的很棒。好的，非常謝謝你。這太有幫助了……

1.en: That is the end of part one. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part one.
1.zh: 第一部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第一部分的答案。

2.en: You will hear an archaeologist who is part of a community project to excavate an ancient village, talking to members of the public who are visiting the site.
2.zh: 你會聽到一位參與社區考古計畫的考古學家，對參觀遺址的民眾介紹發掘古代村莊的工作。

2.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
2.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 11 至 16 題。

2.en: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
2.zh: 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 11 至 16 題。

2.en: Hello, I'm Hayden. I'm one of the archaeologists investigating the site here at Bidcaster.
2.zh: 大家好，我是 Hayden。我是正在調查 Bidcaster 這處遺址的考古學家之一。

2.en: This is the third summer for this community project, and most of the people digging here are volunteers.
2.zh: 這是這個社區計畫進行的第三個夏天，而在這裡發掘的大多數人都是志工。

2.en: I'm a full-time archaeologist for the town council, but I was asked to join the project by NHA, a charity which sets up projects like this up and down the country.
2.zh: 我是鎮議會的全職考古學家， 但我是受 NHA 邀請加入這個計畫的。NHA 是一個慈善機構，在全國各地設立這類計畫。

2.en: As you can see, we're next to Bidcaster Castle, which is great because the owners let us use their facilities.
2.zh: 如你所見，我們就在 Bidcaster Castle 旁邊，這很棒，因為城堡主人讓我們使用他們的設施。

2.en: So, how did we get to where we are today? Many archaeology projects happen when an ancient object is found, and in our case, that object was a gold coin.
2.zh: 那麼，我們是怎麼走到今天這一步的呢？很多考古計畫都是因為發現古代物件而展開的； 在我們的案例中，那件物品是一枚金幣。

2.en: Coins are often found by people using metal detectors to look for things buried in the ground – or coins are uncovered when wild animals like rabbits have been digging tunnels.
2.zh: 硬幣常常是人們用金屬探測器尋找地下埋藏物時發現的，或者是像兔子這類野生動物挖洞時把硬幣翻出來。

2.en: Here, a walker found it on the ground after a rainstorm washed away some of the earth and sand.
2.zh: 在這裡，是一位行人在暴雨沖走部分泥土和沙子後，在地面上發現了它。

2.en: When the story of the gold coin hit the news, Peter Swift, an amateur historian, contacted me to say he believed there had been a village on this site, centuries before the castle was built.
2.zh: 當這枚金幣的消息登上新聞後，業餘歷史學家 Peter Swift 聯絡我，說他相信在城堡建成前幾個世紀，這裡曾經有一座村莊。

2.en: Just by chance, the team found some old maps and documents in our library which showed five-hundred-year-old drawings of ruined buildings on the grassy area between the outer stone walls of the castle and the river.
2.zh: 純屬偶然，團隊在我們的圖書館裡找到一些舊地圖和文件， 上面有 500 年前的圖畫，描繪了城堡外石牆和河流之間草地上的廢墟建築。

2.en: We knew then we were onto something.
2.zh: 那時我們就知道，我們找到了重要線索。

2.en: Over the three summers the team has been here, we've found the remains of several buildings, and more broken pots than you can count!
2.zh: 在團隊來到這裡的三個夏天裡，我們發現了幾棟建築的遺跡，以及多到數不清的陶罐碎片！

2.en: Normally you'd expect to find brooches and other jewellery, but we're still waiting to uncover any such items.
2.zh: 通常你會期待找到胸針和其他首飾，但我們目前還在等待發現這類物品。

2.en: The people who once lived here were skilled at making tools from animal bones, as you'll see when you visit the exhibition.
2.zh: 曾經住在這裡的人很擅長用動物骨頭製作工具，這點你們參觀展覽時會看到。

2.en: Besides the discovery of the village, we've also found evidence of human activity on the other side of the river – no other houses or huts so far, but we can see the borders of an ancient field system.
2.zh: 除了發現這座村莊外，我們也在河對岸發現了人類活動的證據——目前還沒有發現其他房屋或小屋，但我們能看到古代田地系統的邊界。

2.en: At one point we found a long wall and thought it was an ancient palace, but it turned out to be a modern wall.
2.zh: 有一次我們發現一堵長牆，原以為是古代宮殿，結果證明它是一堵現代牆。

2.en: This summer's work will end soon, but we'll be back next summer.
2.zh: 今年夏天的工作很快就會結束，但我們明年夏天還會回來。

2.en: In the meantime, we're putting on a series of guided tours for school groups this autumn.
2.zh: 在此期間，我們今年秋天會為學校團體安排一系列導覽活動。

2.en: Oh and, maybe you saw the TV documentary about our project.
2.zh: 哦，還有，也許你們看過關於我們這個計畫的電視紀錄片。

2.en: That suggested the objects we've found are going to the town's museum, but we don't know that for sure yet.
2.zh: 那部節目暗示我們發現的物品會送到鎮上的博物館，但我們目前還不能確定。

2.en: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
2.zh: 在你聽接下來的演講之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 17 至 20 題。

2.en: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
2.zh: 現在請聆聽並回答第 17 至 20 題。

2.en: When you enter the site, please make sure you keep to the paths at all times.
2.zh: 進入遺址時，請務必始終沿著小路行走。

2.en: There are a few other things – the highlights of the site, if you like – that I want to mention.
2.zh: 我還想提幾個地方——你也可以說是這處遺址的亮點。

2.en: Take a look at the map; our present location is marked at the bottom.
2.zh: 請看一下地圖；我們目前的位置標在底部。

2.en: This year we've identified the foundations of an ancient bridge.
2.zh: 今年我們確認了一座古橋的地基。

2.en: And it's really exciting today because a team of divers are in the river searching for lost objects.
2.zh: 今天特別令人興奮，因為有一隊潛水員正在河裡尋找遺失的物件。

2.en: To reach the bridge, take the main path ahead of you, go straight on and keep going till the path bends to the left.
2.zh: 要到橋那裡，請沿著前方主路直走，一直走到小路向左彎。

2.en: You'll see a smaller track leading off to the right.
2.zh: 你會看到一條較小的小徑向右延伸。

2.en: Follow that to take you to the river, where the divers are.
2.zh: 沿著那條路走，就會到達河邊，也就是潛水員所在的地方。

2.en: You might be interested to see the rubbish pit.
2.zh: 你們可能會有興趣看看垃圾坑。

2.en: This is very near the castle walls in the northwest corner of the site.
2.zh: 它非常靠近遺址西北角的城堡牆。

2.en: It actually dates to the time of the castle and not the ancient village.
2.zh: 它其實屬於城堡時期，而不是古代村莊時期。

2.en: We found oyster shells and fish bones, and we assume they were thrown from the castle kitchen above.
2.zh: 我們發現了牡蠣殼和魚骨，推測它們是從上方的城堡廚房丟下來的。

2.en: One area we excavated in the first summer uncovered the site of a meeting hall.
2.zh: 第一年夏天，我們發掘的一個區域揭露了一座會議廳的遺址。

2.en: We knew it was an important building because it had two rows of post holes, deep enough to support a large roof.
2.zh: 我們知道那是一座重要建築， 因為那裡有兩排柱洞，深度足以支撐大型屋頂。

2.en: It's the largest structure in the central area of the site, next to the current excavation area.
2.zh: 它是遺址中央區域最大的結構，就在目前發掘區旁邊。

2.en: Last year we discovered a fish pond in the ancient village.
2.zh: 去年，我們在古代村莊中發現了一個魚塘。

2.en: Normally these were beside a river.
2.zh: 通常這類魚塘會在河邊。

2.en: The pond here is further away, but it's possible the river has moved slightly.
2.zh: 這裡的魚塘離河較遠，不過也有可能是河道稍微移動過。

2.en: Anyway, to get there from here, you turn right at the first information board you come to, and follow the path into the trees.
2.zh: 總之，從這裡去那裡時，在你遇到的第一塊資訊牌處右轉， 然後沿著小路走進樹林。

2.en: Before you come out of the trees, you'll see it on your right.
2.zh: 在你走出樹林之前，你會在右手邊看到它。

2.en: If you reach the river, you've gone too far.
2.zh: 如果你走到河邊，那就走太遠了。

2.en: So, does anyone…
2.zh: 那麼，有沒有人……

2.en: That is the end of part two. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.
2.zh: 第二部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第二部分的答案。

3.en: You will hear two theatre studies students, Maya and Finn, discussing their project on theater programs.
3.zh: 你會聽到兩位戲劇研究學生 Maya 和 Finn 討論他們關於劇場節目單的專題。

3.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26.
3.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 21 至 26 題。

3.en: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26.
3.zh: 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 21 至 26 題。

3.en: MAYA: So Finn, I've done as much as I can for our project on theatre programmes. How's your research coming along?
3.zh: Maya：Finn，我已經盡力完成我們關於劇場節目單專題的部分了。 你的研究進行得怎麼樣？

3.en: FINN: OK, Maya. I didn't know theatre programmes are called playbills in the USA till I started looking into the topic.
3.zh: Finn：還可以，Maya。我開始研究這個題目後，才知道劇場節目單在美國叫 playbills。

3.en: Even though I struggled to find many useful websites, I'm glad we picked this subject.
3.zh: 雖然我很難找到很多有用的網站，但我很高興我們選了這個主題。

3.en: No one else on the course is doing the same as us, although it is one of the research areas of the module convenor.
3.zh: 課程裡沒有其他人做和我們一樣的題目，雖然這是該模組負責人的研究領域之一。

3.en: MAYA: That might actually put some people off.
3.zh: Maya：那其實可能會讓一些人卻步。

3.en: FINN: I suppose so. Anyway, I hadn't realised there are actually companies specialising in creating theatre programmes.
3.zh: Finn：我想也是。不管怎樣，我之前沒意識到其實有專門製作劇場節目單的公司。

3.en: MAYA: Yes, they're quite common nowadays.
3.zh: Maya：是的，現在相當常見。

3.en: Contrary to what many people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes, in fact companies buy the rights to publish programmes on the theatre's behalf – and then make their money selling advertising space within the programme booklet.
3.zh: 和許多人以為的相反，劇院並不是雇人製作節目單；事實上，公司會購買代表劇院出版節目單的權利，然後透過出售節目冊中的廣告版面賺錢。

3.en: FINN: It must be easier for theatres to do it that way.
3.zh: Finn：對劇院來說，這樣做一定比較容易。

3.en: MAYA: Yes.
3.zh: Maya：是的。

3.en: FINN: I remember reading something about programmes in early British theatre.
3.zh: Finn：我記得讀過一些關於早期英國劇場節目單的資料。

3.en: It said that the cast was always very important.
3.zh: 裡面說演員陣容一直非常重要。

3.en: MAYA: Yeah, audiences were very familiar with leading actors, and big names would draw huge crowds.
3.zh: Maya：是啊，觀眾對主要演員非常熟悉，而知名演員會吸引大量人潮。

3.en: FINN: But I hadn't realised that if the programme named a famous actor, that's who the public expected to perform.
3.zh: Finn：但我之前沒意識到，如果節目單上列出某位知名演員，觀眾就會期待那個人上台演出。

3.en: And if that didn't happen, people accused the theatre of breaking their agreement with the audience.
3.zh: 如果沒有發生，人們就會指責劇院違反了和觀眾之間的約定。

3.en: They would demand refunds, and, if they didn't get them, there were riots!
3.zh: 他們會要求退款；如果拿不到退款，就會發生騷亂！

3.en: MAYA: Outrageous. That'd never happen now.
3.zh: Maya：太誇張了。現在絕不會發生這種事。

3.en: FINN: No, people are too polite, even when they're disappointed if the star of the show misses a performance.
3.zh: Finn：不會，現在的人太有禮貌了，即使主演缺席演出讓他們失望也是如此。

3.en: MAYA: We should definitely include that information about early audiences in our project.
3.zh: Maya：我們絕對應該把早期觀眾的這些資訊放進專題裡。

3.en: I also think it's important to mention that lots of ordinary people at that time were illiterate, so theatre programmes were of limited value in advertising plays.
3.zh: 我也覺得有必要提到，當時很多普通人不識字，所以劇場節目單在宣傳戲劇方面的價值有限。

3.en: When a company of actors arrived in a town, they'd parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances.
3.zh: 當一個劇團來到城鎮時，他們會穿著戲服在街上遊行、敲鼓，並宣布即將上演的劇目。

3.en: FINN: Interesting. I couldn't imagine that happening now either.
3.zh: Finn：真有意思。我也無法想像現在還會發生這種事。

3.en: MAYA: There's also an interesting comparison to make between eighteenth and nineteenth-century programmes.
3.zh: Maya：18 世紀和 19 世紀的節目單之間也有一個有趣的比較。

3.en: FINN: Wasn't it in the nineteenth century that theatre programmes started to resemble programmes today?
3.zh: Finn：劇場節目單不是在 19 世紀開始變得像今天的節目單嗎？

3.en: MAYA: Yes. And, unlike programmes from the eighteenth century, they always used colour.
3.zh: Maya：是的。而且和 18 世紀的節目單不同，它們總是使用色彩。

3.en: FINN: And there was a greater variety of designs.
3.zh: Finn：而且設計種類也更多。

3.en: But personally, I think eighteenth-century programmes were superior because they told the theatre-goers so many things, including about the actors.
3.zh: 但就我個人而言，我認為 18 世紀的節目單更好，因為它們告訴觀眾很多資訊，包括演員方面的內容。

3.en: MAYA: And about the writer, the plot, and sometimes the history of the play.
3.zh: Maya：還有作者、劇情，有時也包括這齣戲的歷史。

3.en: FINN: That's right… What should we say about theatre programmes in the twentieth century?
3.zh: Finn：沒錯……那我們該怎麼談 20 世紀的劇場節目單呢？

3.en: MAYA: I reckon the most important thing is the dramatic change they underwent during World War Two.
3.zh: Maya：我覺得最重要的是，它們在第二次世界大戰期間經歷了巨大的變化。

3.en: FINN: When the government imposed restrictions on the use of paper.
3.zh: Finn：也就是政府限制紙張使用的時候。

3.en: MAYA: Yeah, but that was only in the UK. In the USA, programmes – or rather, playbills – continued to be published in the same format ...
3.zh: Maya：是的，但那只發生在英國。 在美國，節目單——或者更準確地說，playbills——仍然以相同形式出版……

3.en: FINN: … while here in the UK, programmes became merely a single sheet of paper folded to create four pages for text.
3.zh: Finn：……而在英國，節目單只剩下一張紙，對摺後形成四頁文字。

3.en: MAYA: What I don't really get is that, after the war, they didn't go back to being more than one sheet, or change in any way for over twenty-five years.
3.zh: Maya：我真正不明白的是，戰後它們沒有恢復成多張紙，也在超過 25 年的時間裡沒有任何變化。

3.en: I know there were paper shortages after the war, but only for five or ten years.
3.zh: 我知道戰後曾有紙張短缺，但那只持續了五到十年。

3.en: FINN: Strange.
3.zh: Finn：真奇怪。

3.en: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.
3.zh: 在你聽接下來的討論之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 27 至 30 題。

3.en: Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30.
3.zh: 現在請聆聽並回答第 27 至 30 題。

3.en: MAYA: I've got some pictures of programmes we could include on the slides for our presentation.
3.zh: Maya：我有一些節目單的圖片，可以放進我們簡報的投影片裡。

3.en: FINN: I found a couple too, Maya. Let's go through and see what we think.
3.zh: Finn：我也找到幾張，Maya。我們一起看一下，看看想法如何。

3.en: MAYA: Erm …, this is an old one, for a play called Ruy Blas.
3.zh: Maya：嗯……這是一張舊的，是一齣叫 Ruy Blas 的戲的節目單。

3.en: FINN: Never heard of that, but the programme looks very decorative.
3.zh: Finn：我從沒聽過那齣戲，但這張節目單看起來很有裝飾性。

3.en: MAYA: Good enough to put in a frame on the wall. The images are just beautiful. Finn, what did you find?
3.zh: Maya：漂亮到可以裝框掛在牆上。 那些圖像真的很美。Finn，你找到什麼？

3.en: FINN: I've got some pages from a programme for Man of La Mancha.
3.zh: Finn：我找到幾頁《Man of La Mancha》的節目單。

3.en: I thought this was a good programme to show, not because of the pictures, but because it contains articles written by members of the theatre company.
3.zh: 我覺得這是一份很值得展示的節目單，不是因為圖片，而是因為裡面有劇團成員寫的文章。

3.en: So we can learn how the production was created, and the thoughts and feelings of the cast.
3.zh: 所以我們可以了解這部作品是如何創作的，以及演員們的想法和感受。

3.en: MAYA: Good. I've got a copy of a programme that's now in a museum.
3.zh: Maya：很好。我有一份目前收藏在博物館裡的節目單副本。

3.en: It's for The Tragedy of Jane Shore and it's said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press.
3.zh: 它是《The Tragedy of Jane Shore》 的節目單，據說是澳洲第一台印刷機印出的、現存最早的文件。

3.en: FINN: Fantastic.
3.zh: Finn：太棒了。

3.en: MAYA: Another programme to talk about is for The Sailors' Festival.
3.zh: Maya：另一份可以談的是《The Sailors' Festival》的節目單。

3.en: It comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago.
3.zh: 它來自大英圖書館幾年前開始建立的節目單數位化館藏。

3.en: It already comprises over two hundred thousand programmes, which is amazing.
3.zh: 這個館藏已經包含超過 20 萬份節目單，真的很驚人。

3.en: FINN: Wish I'd known about it while I was doing my research!
3.zh: Finn：真希望我做研究時就知道這個！

3.en: That is the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three.
3.zh: 第三部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第三部分的答案。

4.en: You will hear a design and technology lecturer talking about inclusive design.
4.zh: 你會聽到一位設計與科技講師談論包容性設計。

4.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
4.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 31 至 40 題。

4.en: Now, listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
4.zh: 現在，請仔細聆聽並回答第 31 至 40 題。

4.en: It's only relatively recently that designers have become aware of the need to be inclusive when designing products.
4.zh: 直到相對近年，設計師才開始意識到在設計產品時需要具備包容性。

4.en: But what does that mean exactly? Well, it simply means designing products that span economic, social and cultural barriers.
4.zh: 但這到底是什麼意思呢？簡單來說，就是設計能跨越經濟、社會和文化障礙的產品。

4.en: It means making sure products are accessible – so that as many different types of people as possible can use them without any type of adaptation having to be made to the original design.
4.zh: 這意味著要確保產品易於使用，讓盡可能多不同類型的人都能使用，而不需要對原始設計進行任何改造。

4.en: Inclusive design is often linked with universal design, although they are not quite the same thing.
4.zh: 包容性設計常常和通用設計聯繫在一起，雖然兩者並不完全相同。

4.en: Universal design aims to make products that work for everyone and that includes considering the needs of people who have cognitive difficulties, which can present quite a challenge.
4.zh: 通用設計旨在製作適合所有人使用的產品，其中包括考慮有認知困難者的需求，而這可能相當具有挑戰性。

4.en: Today, examples of successful inclusive design can be seen all around us.
4.zh: 如今，我們周圍到處都可以看到成功的包容性設計案例。

4.en: In workplaces it is common to see desks which can be adjusted to suit people of different heights or for wheelchair users.
4.zh: 在工作場所，常可以看到可調整高度的桌子，以適應不同身高的人或輪椅使用者。

4.en: This still isn't always the case, however, and is one reason why office workers often suffer from back or neck problems.
4.zh: 不過，情況並不總是如此，這也是辦公室工作者常常出現背部或頸部問題的原因之一。

4.en: You'll find another example in the public toilets of countless hotels, airports and offices.
4.zh: 你也可以在無數飯店、機場和辦公室的公共廁所裡看到另一個例子。

4.en: Taps that you activate by sensor require no pressing or twisting movements.
4.zh: 感應式水龍頭不需要按壓或旋轉動作。

4.en: These are not only more hygienic, they're also easier for people with dexterity or mobility issues.
4.zh: 它們不僅更衛生，對手部靈活度或行動能力有困難的人來說也更容易使用。

4.en: The tech industry has been criticised in the past for focusing too much on young consumers but this is changing.
4.zh: 科技產業過去曾因過度關注年輕消費者而受到批評，但這種情況正在改變。

4.en: Many products are now designed with the elderly in mind.
4.zh: 現在許多產品在設計時都會考慮老年人的需求。

4.en: For example, it's well known that vision declines with age, and that we also become worse at distinguishing between similar colours; in particular, shades of blue, which is why software designers rarely create interfaces with this colour.
4.zh: 例如，眾所周知，視力會隨著年齡增長而下降，而且我們分辨相近顏色的能力也會變差； 尤其是藍色系，因此軟體設計師很少使用這種顏色來設計介面。

4.en: Motor skills also decline with age and some people have difficulty doing everyday things like picking up a cup or opening a door.
4.zh: 動作能力也會隨年齡下降，有些人在做日常事情時會遇到困難，例如拿起杯子或開門。

4.en: This can also affect their ability to use a mouse or keyboard.
4.zh: 這也可能影響他們使用滑鼠或鍵盤的能力。

4.en: So voice access is now a routine way of making commands.
4.zh: 因此，語音控制現在已成為發出指令的一種常見方式。

4.en: It's worth looking at the problems non-inclusive designs cause when not enough consideration is given to a range of users, as it can have a serious impact on people's lives.
4.zh: 當設計沒有充分考慮不同使用者時，非包容性設計會造成許多問題，這點值得關注，因為它可能對人們的生活造成嚴重影響。

4.en: Access is one obvious example because it has such a huge impact on disabled people's independence.
4.zh: 使用權就是一個明顯例子，因為它對身心障礙者的獨立生活有巨大影響。

4.en: Not being able to access public transport because buses or trains are not wheelchair-friendly means many disabled people can't go out unless someone goes with them.
4.zh: 如果公車或火車不適合輪椅使用者，導致無法搭乘公共交通，這就意味著許多身心障礙者除非有人陪同，否則無法外出。

4.en: Safety is another issue.
4.zh: 安全是另一個問題。

4.en: Inexplicably, most cars are still crash-tested using a dummy based on an average-sized male.
4.zh: 令人難以理解的是，大多數汽車在碰撞測試時，仍使用以平均身材男性為基準的假人。

4.en: This has safety implications for all women, particularly those who are pregnant, as the seatbelts worn by the dummy are not adapted to accommodate them.
4.zh: 這對所有女性都有安全影響， 尤其是孕婦，因為測試假人使用的安全帶並未調整到能適合她們。

4.en: Over the past 100 years, workplaces in the UK have, on the whole, become considerably safer.
4.zh: 過去 100 年來，英國工作場所整體而言已變得安全許多。

4.en: Employers are legally required to provide well-maintained personal protective equipment or PPE – anything from goggles to full body suits – to workers who need it, free of charge.
4.zh: 法律要求雇主免費為有需要的員工提供維護良好的個人防護裝備，也就是 PPE，範圍從護目鏡到全身防護服都有。

4.en: But most PPE is designed to fit men.
4.zh: 但是，大多數個人防護裝備都是依照男性身形設計的。

4.en: A recent report found that employers often think that when it comes to female workers, all they need to do to comply with this legal requirement is to buy jackets, for example, designed for a small man.
4.zh: 最近一份報告發現，雇主常常認為，對女性員工而言，要符合法律要求，只需要購買例如為小個子男性設計的外套即可。

4.en: The problem with this is that women can be tall and still have much smaller shoulders than the average man.
4.zh: 問題在於，女性即使身材高挑，肩膀仍可能比一般男性窄得多。

4.en: Ill-fitting PPE such as hi-vis jackets, vests and body armour can put women at risk.
4.zh: 不合身的個人防護裝備，例如高能見度外套、背心和防彈護具，可能會讓女性處於危險之中。

4.en: The report found that 95% of women said that their PPE often hampered their work and that this problem was worst in the emergency services, particularly the police.
4.zh: 報告發現，95% 的女性表示，她們的個人防護裝備經常妨礙工作；這個問題在緊急服務部門最嚴重，尤其是在警察部門。

4.en: Another problem is related to comfort at work.
4.zh: 另一個問題與工作時的舒適度有關。

4.en: A very common scenario in offices in summertime is to see women wrapped in blankets or wearing sweaters while the air conditioning is on high.
4.zh: 夏天的辦公室裡很常見的一幕是，空調開得很強，女性裹著毯子或穿著毛衣。

4.en: Meanwhile the men are in shorts and T-shirts.
4.zh: 與此同時，男性則穿著短褲和 T 恤。

4.en: This is due to differences in metabolic rates for men and women.
4.zh: 這是因為男性和女性的新陳代謝率不同。

4.en: There is a standard setting for air conditioning to be at a temperature of 21 degrees, designed to suit men, and in most modern offices it's not possible to turn the air conditioning up or down.
4.zh: 空調有一個標準設定溫度是 21 度，而這是為了適合男性；在大多數現代辦公室裡，空調也無法自行調高或調低。

4.en: This means that many offices which mainly employ women are wasting energy by having the air conditioning set too high.
4.zh: 這意味著許多主要雇用女性的辦公室，因為空調設定過強而浪費能源。

4.en: As you can see from the examples I've just mentioned, there are serious consequences for designs which don't consider the needs of all users. This is …
4.zh: 從我剛才提到的例子可以看出，沒有考慮所有使用者需求的設計會帶來嚴重後果。這是……

4.en: That is the end of part four. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part four.
4.zh: 第四部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第四部分的答案。

1.explanation: 題目寫：“Prices range from $105 to $ _____ per room per month”，意思是每個房間每月租金由 105 美元至多少。 錄音說：“starts at a hundred and five dollars and goes up to two hundred and thirty-nine dollars.” “goes up to” 對應題目的 “range from … to …”，所以價格上限是 239。 中伏位：105 已經印在題目中，是最低價；空格問的是最高價。題目亦已經有 $，所以只需要填 239 ，不用再寫 dollars。

2.explanation: 題目寫：“The furniture is very _____”，問的是 Peak Rentals 家具本身的特點。 錄音說：“the furniture from Peak Rentals is more modern than any of the other companies.” “more modern than any of the other companies” 表示它的家具相比其他公司更加現代，所以填 modern 。 中伏位：錄音亦提到 “positive reports” 和 “delivered … in one or two days”，但前者是公司評價，後者是送貨速度；這一格問的是 furniture 本身怎樣。modern 是形容詞，放在 “very modern” 文法正確。

3.explanation: 題目寫：“Special offer: free _____ with every living room set”，問租客廳家具時免費得到甚麼。 錄音說：“If you rent living room furniture … you'll also get a lamp at no extra cost.” “at no extra cost” = free；“living room furniture” 對應 “living room set”，所以免費贈品是 lamp。 中伏位：錄音提到 “a set of chairs and a TV table”，但這些是客廳家具組本身，不是額外免費送的東西。真正的 special offer 是 lamp。

4.explanation: 題目的公司名稱寫：“_____ and Oliver”。 錄音說：“Then you could try Aaron and Oliver.” 女士沒有聽清楚後，男士再拼字：“Aaron. Double-A-R-O-N.” 所以空格只需要填 Aaron。 中伏位：這是一道拼字題，不能只靠發音猜。錄音特別提醒開頭是 “Double-A”，即 A-A-R-O-N，不要寫成 Aron、Arron 等。題目已有 “and Oliver”，亦不用重寫整個公司名。

5.explanation: 題目寫：“12% monthly fee for _____”，即這個每月額外 12% 的費用是為了甚麼。 錄音說：“they charge an extra twelve per cent every month in case of damage.” “in case of damage” 表示為可能出現的家具損壞作保障，所以表格改寫成 “fee for damage”。 中伏位：錄音之後提到 cleaning service，但那是公司另外提供的一項服務，與這個 12% monthly fee 無關。damage 是名詞，填入後意思完整。

6.explanation: 題目寫：“cheapest prices for renting furniture and _____ items”。 錄音說 Larch Furniture “has the lowest prices in town”，而且：“That's for both furniture and also electronic equipment.” “electronic equipment” 被題目改寫成 “electronic items”，所以空格填 electronic。 中伏位：不能填 equipment，因為題目後面已經有 items；“equipment items” 並不自然。空格需要一個形容詞修飾 items，所以 electronic 最符合文法。

7.explanation: 題目寫：“Must have own _____”，意思是使用 Larch Furniture 時，顧客必須自己安排甚麼。 錄音說：“you have to take out insurance on the furniture, and you need to organise that yourself.” “organise that yourself” 正好對應題目的 “own”，即保險是顧客自己安排，所以答案是 insurance。 中伏位：錄音之後還說 minimum contract 是 six months，但那已經對應表格下一項，不是 “Must have own _____”。

8.explanation: 題目公司的名稱寫：“_____ Rentals”。 錄音直接說：“It's called Space Rentals.” 所以題目已經提供 Rentals，空格只填 Space。 中伏位：錄音緊接著說公司 “located very near to the house”，這只是位置資訊，不是名稱的一部分。

9.explanation: 題目寫：“See the _____ for the most up-to-date prices”，意思是要到哪裡查看最新收費。 錄音說：“I don't have any information about their charges, so it's best to use their app to find out what it would cost you.” “find out what it would cost” 就是查看價格，因此要看的是 app。 中伏位：charges / cost 都有出現在錄音，但題目不是問「價格叫甚麼」，是去哪裡查看價格。 所以答案是 app。

10.explanation: 題目寫：“**_____ are allowed within 7 days of delivery.” 錄音說：“if you don't like the furniture once it's delivered, you can request exchanges – as long as you do that within a week of receiving it.” “within a week” = within 7 days；“can request” 對應 “are allowed”，所以答案是 exchanges。 中伏位：錄音沒有說 refunds 或 returns，明確說 exchanges，即更換家具。 題目用 “are allowed”，主語需要複數，所以填 exchanges。

11.explanation: 題目問：誰負責開始這個 community project？ 錄音說 Hayden 是 “a full-time archaeologist for the town council”，但他接著說自己 “was asked to join the project by NHA, a charity which sets up projects like this up and down the country.” 關鍵是 “sets up projects” = starts / establishes projects；而 “up and down the country” 表示這個慈善機構在全國運作，所以對應 a national charity。 中伏位：local council 是 Hayden 的僱主，不代表 council 創立計畫；castle owners 只是讓考古團隊使用設施。真正 “sets up projects” 的是 NHA，所以選 B。

12.answer: A — Heavy rain had removed some of the soil
12.explanation: 題目問：這枚 gold coin 實際上是怎樣被發現的？ 錄音先說硬幣一般可能由 metal detector 使用者找到，亦可能被 rabbits 挖出；但接著明確說這個個案： “Here, a walker found it on the ground after a rainstorm washed away some of the earth and sand.” “rainstorm washed away some of the earth” = heavy rain removed some of the soil，所以選 A。 中伏位：metal detectors 和 rabbits 都真的有在錄音中出現，但那只是講「硬幣一般怎樣被發現」。關鍵詞 Here 把內容轉回 Bidcaster 這一次真正發生的情況。

13.answer: A — the lucky discovery of old records
13.explanation: 題目問：甚麼令考古學家相信這裡曾有一條 ancient village？ 錄音說團隊 “by chance” 在圖書館找到 “old maps and documents”，當中有五百年前 ruined buildings 的圖畫，之後說： “We knew then we were onto something.” “old maps and documents” = old records；“by chance” 對應 lucky discovery，所以答案是 A。 中伏位：Peter Swift 的確先提出相信這裡曾有村莊，但題目問的是甚麼 led the archaeologists to believe。真正讓團隊有實質證據的是之後偶然找到的歷史資料。

14.explanation: 題目問：考古團隊現在仍然希望找到甚麼？ 錄音說他們已經找到 building remains 和大量 broken pots，接著說： “Normally you'd expect to find brooches and other jewellery, but we're still waiting to uncover any such items.” “still waiting to uncover” = still hoping to find，所以答案是 C — pieces of jewellery。 中伏位：pottery 已經找到 “more broken pots than you can count”；animal bones 亦已經出現在 exhibition 中。只有 jewellery 是他們仍然未找到、仍在等待的東西。

15.explanation: 題目問：在城堡河對岸發現了甚麼？ 錄音說： “on the other side of the river … no other houses or huts so far, but we can see the borders of an ancient field system.” “borders of an ancient field system” = the outline of fields，所以答案是 B。 中伏位：C 的 huts 被錄音直接否定：“no … huts so far”。至於 palace，他們曾把一堵長牆誤以為 palace， 但最後發現只是 modern wall，因此 A 亦不對。

16.answer: C — start to organise school visits
16.explanation: 題目問：今年夏天的發掘工作結束後，團隊計劃做甚麼？ 錄音說： “This summer's work will end soon … In the meantime, we're putting on a series of guided tours for school groups this autumn.” “guided tours for school groups” 對應 school visits，因此選 C。 中伏位：TV documentary 已經播放過，不是未來計畫。至於 museum，錄音只說電視節目曾暗示物件會送到博物館，但 “we don't know that for sure yet”，所以不是確定計畫。

17.explanation: 題目要根據地圖找出 bridge foundations 的位置。 錄音給出的路線是： “go straight on … till the path bends to the left. You'll see a smaller track leading off to the right. Follow that to take you to the river.” 所以要從 “You are here” 沿主路向前，到主路左彎的位置，再走右邊的小徑到河旁。地圖上符合這段路線的位置是 B。 中伏位：這題真正決定位置的是 path bends left → smaller track right → river，不要只因為某個標記靠近中央 excavation area 就選它。

18.explanation: 題目要找 rubbish pit。 錄音說： “This is very near the castle walls in the northwest corner of the site.” 地圖中 north 是上方、west 是左方，所以 northwest = 左上方；靠近 castle walls 的左上位置是 A。 中伏位：其他位置也可能靠近 castle walls，但題目不是只說 near the walls，非常具體地說 northwest corner。方位詞才是決定答案的關鍵。

19.explanation: 錄音說 meeting hall： “It's the largest structure in the central area of the site, next to the current excavation area.” 因此要同時滿足兩個條件： central area + next to current excavation area 地圖中 G 位於中央，而且緊鄰 “Site of current dig”，亦符合 largest structure 的描述，所以答案是 G。 中伏位：只看到 “central area” 還不夠；還要利用 “next to the current excavation area” 進一步鎖定位置。

20.explanation: 錄音說： “turn right at the first information board … follow the path into the trees. Before you come out of the trees, you'll see it on your right. If you reach the river, you've gone too far.” 所以路線是：第一塊 information board 右轉 → 進樹林 → 還沒走出樹林前，右邊便是 fish pond。 地圖上符合的是 E。 中伏位：錄音特別說 “If you reach the river, you've gone too far”，所以不能選已經太接近或到達河邊的位置。

21.answer: B — had not been chosen by other students
21.explanation: 題目問：Finn 很高興發現他們的題目有甚麼特點。 錄音說： “I'm glad we picked this subject. No one else on the course is doing the same as us.” “No one else … is doing the same” = the topic had not been chosen by other students，所以選 B。 中伏位：A 不對，因為 Finn 明確說這其實是 module convenor 的 research area，對方並非不熟悉。C 也不對，因為 Finn 說自己 “struggled to find many useful websites”，顯示研究並不容易。

22.answer: A — theatres pay companies to produce them
22.explanation: 題目問：Maya 說人們對 theatre programmes 有甚麼 mistaken belief。 錄音明確用： “Contrary to what many people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes; in fact companies buy the rights to publish programmes…” “Contrary to what many people think” 已經直接指出接下來是在糾正常見誤解。人們以為 theatres hire / pay companies to produce programmes，但實際上是公司向 theatre 購買出版權，所以答案是 A。 中伏位：advertising 的確有提到，但錄音是解釋那些公司如何賺錢。

23.answer: C — were seen as a kind of contract
23.explanation: 題目問：Finn 對 early British theatre programmes 的甚麼事情感到驚訝。 錄音說 Finn “hadn't realised” 如果 programme 寫明某位 famous actor，觀眾便期待那人一定演出；如果沒有演出，觀眾會指責 theatre： “breaking their agreement with the audience.” “agreement with the audience” 表示 programme 上列出的演員名單被視為一種承諾，近似 contract，所以答案是 C。 中伏位：錄音沒有說 programme 免費派發，也沒有說觀眾很難取得它。真正令 Finn 驚訝的是它具有近似合約承諾的作用。

24.explanation: 題目問：Maya 認為專題應該解釋，當時的 actor companies 為甚麼要怎樣做。 錄音先說很多普通人 illiterate，所以 theatre programmes 在 “advertising plays” 方面價值有限。於是劇團會： “parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances.” “announcing upcoming performances” 就是 promoting their own plays，所以答案是 A。 中伏位：錄音說劇團 “arrived in a town”，但這不是在解釋為何他們要 tour；這整段重點是：因為 programme 廣告作用有限，所以需要用街頭方式宣傳演出。

25.explanation: 題目比較 eighteenth-century 和 nineteenth-century programmes，問兩位學生認為十八世紀的版本有甚麼優點。 Finn 說： “eighteenth-century programmes were superior because they told the theatre-goers so many things…” Maya 接著補充，包括 writer、plot 和 history of the play。 “told … so many things” = more informative，所以答案是 C。 中伏位：錄音中的 colour 和 greater variety of designs 是十九世紀 programmes 的特點，所以 B “more colourful” 的方向剛好相反。題目問的是十八世紀相較之下有甚麼優點。

26.answer: B — British theatre programmes failed to develop for so long
26.explanation: 題目問：Maya 在 twentieth century 的發展中，有甚麼事情 “doesn't fully understand”。 錄音中她直接說： “What I don't really get is that, after the war, they didn't go back to being more than one sheet, or change in any way for over twenty-five years.” “didn't … change in any way for over twenty-five years” = failed to develop for so long，所以答案是 B。 中伏位：美國 programmes 並不是很少出版；錄音反而說它們 continued in the same format。亦沒有說英國 programme copied fashions from the USA。

27.explanation: 題目問 Ruy Blas 的 programme 有甚麼評語。 錄音說： “the programme looks very decorative.” Maya 再說： “Good enough to put in a frame on the wall. The images are just beautiful.” 可以裝框掛在牆上，而且圖像非常漂亮，意思就是這份 programme 像一件藝術品，所以選 F。 中伏位：錄音確實說它是 “an old one”，但選項沒有單純「很古老」；真正能準確對應描述的是 artwork。

28.answer: E — It contains insights into the show
28.explanation: 題目問 Man of La Mancha 的 programme 有甚麼特色。 Finn 說： “not because of the pictures, but because it contains articles written by members of the theatre company.” 因此讀者可以了解： “how the production was created, and the thoughts and feelings of the cast.” 這些都是對演出製作過程及演員想法的深入資料，即 insights into the show，所以答案是 E。 中伏位：Finn 特別說 “not because of the pictures”，所以不能因為 programme 有圖片而選 F artwork。

29.answer: B — It is historically significant for a country
29.explanation: 題目問 The Tragedy of Jane Shore 的 programme 有甚麼評語。 錄音說： “it is said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press.” 它與 Australia's first printing press 有關，而且被認為是現存最早由該印刷機印出的文件，因此對澳洲具有重要歷史價值，正好對應 historically significant for a country。 所以答案是 B。 中伏位：錄音也說這份 programme 現在收藏於 museum，但「在博物館」本身不是選項；真正決定答案的是它和澳洲印刷史的關係。

30.answer: D — It is included in a recent project
30.explanation: 題目問 The Sailors' Festival 的 programme 有甚麼評語。 錄音說： “It comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago.” “started a few years ago” 表示這是一個較近期開始的 project；該 programme 是這個 digitised collection 的一部分。 所以答案是 D — It is included in a recent project。 中伏位：沒有提到它特別吸引 audiences，也沒有討論來源是否 controversial。真正的定位詞是 digitised collection + started a few years ago。

31.explanation: 題目寫： “Designing products … without the need for any _____.” 錄音說： “as many different types of people as possible can use them without any type of adaptation having to be made to the original design.” 題目的 “without the need for any …” 幾乎直接改寫錄音的 “without any type of adaptation”，所以答案是 adaptation。 中伏位：“original design” 是被改動的對象，不是「不需要的東西」。adaptation 是名詞，放在 “any adaptation” 文法亦正確。

32.explanation: 題目寫： “people with _____ problems.” 錄音說 universal design 需要考慮： “people who have cognitive difficulties.” “difficulties” = problems，所以 “cognitive difficulties” 被改寫成 “cognitive problems”，答案是 cognitive。 中伏位：前面 economic、social、cultural barriers 是 inclusive design 定義的一部分；這一格位於 universal design 的說明中，要跟著題目所在段落定位。

33.explanation: 題目寫： “_____ which are adjustable, avoiding back or neck problems.” 錄音說： “In workplaces it is common to see desks which can be adjusted…” 之後又提到不合適的工作設置是 office workers 出現 “back or neck problems” 的原因之一。 “desks which can be adjusted” = desks which are adjustable，所以答案是 desks。 題目用 “which are”，亦提示前面的名詞是複數形式。

34.explanation: 題目寫： “**_____ in public toilets which are easier to use.” 錄音說： “Taps that you activate by sensor require no pressing or twisting movements … they're also easier for people with dexterity or mobility issues.” 題目的 “in public toilets” 和 “easier to use” 都直接對應這段，所以答案是 taps。 中伏位：sensor 只是 taps 的操作方式。題目問的是「甚麼東西」比較容易使用，因此答案是物件 taps ，不是 sensor。

35.explanation: 題目寫： “designers avoid using _____ in interfaces.” 錄音說年紀增加後，人較難分辨相近顏色： “in particular, shades of blue, which is why software designers rarely create interfaces with this colour.” “rarely create interfaces with this colour” = avoid using blue in interfaces，所以答案是 blue。 中伏位：錄音特別指出 blue。題目亦要求 ONE WORD ONLY，所以直接填顏色名稱。

36.explanation: 題目寫： “people can make commands using a mouse, keyboard or their _____.” 錄音說部分長者難以使用 mouse or keyboard，因此： “voice access is now a routine way of making commands.” voice access 的意思就是用 voice 發出指令，所以空格填 voice。 中伏位：不能填 access，因為題目句型是 “using … their _____”；自然意思是 “using their voice”。

37.explanation: 題目寫： “Seatbelts are especially problematic for _____ women.” 錄音說，以男性身形為基準的 crash-test dummy 對所有女性都有安全影響： “particularly those who are pregnant, as the seatbelts … are not adapted to accommodate them.” “particularly” = especially，所以題目的特定女性群體就是 pregnant women。 中伏位：錄音先說 all women，但題目有控制詞 especially，因此不能只理解為普通 women；要找被特別指出的群體：pregnant women。

38.explanation: 題目寫： “PPE jackets are often unsuitable because of the size of women's _____.” 錄音解釋，即使女性身材高挑： “women can be tall and still have much smaller shoulders than the average man.” 所以問題在於女性 shoulders 的尺寸與按男性身形設計的 PPE 不一致，答案是 shoulders。 中伏位：錄音有提到 “small man”，但題目問的是女性身體哪個部位的 size 造成不合身，所以要填 shoulders。

39.explanation: 題目寫： “PPE for female _____ officers dealing with emergencies is the worst.” 錄音說： “this problem was worst in the emergency services, particularly the police.” “particularly the police” 指出在 emergency services 中，問題最嚴重的是 police。因此放入題目便成為固定搭配： police officers 所以答案是 police。 中伏位：題目已經用 “dealing with emergencies” 表達 emergency services 的概念，所以不能再填 emergency；空格需要和 officers 組成職業名稱。

40.explanation: 題目寫： “The _____ in offices is often too low for women.” 錄音說辦公室空調通常採用： “a temperature of 21 degrees, designed to suit men.” 前面亦描述夏天女性常常裹著毯子或穿 sweater，表示室內對她們而言太冷。因此題目的 “too low” 指的是 temperature 太低。 中伏位：錄音最後說 air conditioning is “set too high”，很容易令人想填 air conditioning。但 air conditioning 設得太強 → temperature 太低。題目的文法是 “The _____ is too low”，真正可以 high / low 的數值是 temperature，所以答案是 temperature。
